expected.note: Path param username is f-string-interpolated into raw SQL via text(); unauthenticated GET /users/v1/{username} allows UNION extraction (e.g. plaintext passwords).
Hardcoded, guessable SECRET_KEY 'random' signs HS256 JWTs; attacker forges a token with sub=admin and impersonates any user.
Unauthenticated GET /users/v1/_debug returns json_debug() for all users (plaintext passwords + admin flag); active even when vuln=0.
PUT /users/v1/{username}/password updates the user named in the path, not the token subject; any logged-in user resets admin's password (account takeover).
Client-supplied 'admin' field in registration body is honored; self-registered user becomes admin (can then delete users).
GET /books/v1/{book_title} looks up by title only (no owner filter) and returns secret_content; any user reads other users' book secrets (titles listed publicly).
Login returns distinct messages for unknown username vs wrong password, enabling username enumeration and targeted password guessing.
Email regex has nested quantifier ([-.\w]*[0-9a-zA-Z])*; ~30-char crafted email (e.g. 'a'*30+'!') causes exponential backtracking, blocking the worker.
Unauthenticated GET /createdb drops all tables and reseeds known users (admin/pass1); anyone can wipe data and restore default admin credentials.
Passwords stored and compared in plaintext (no hashing); any DB read (SQLi, debug endpoint) yields reusable credentials.
Seeded admin account with weak hardcoded password 'pass1' (also documented in spec); attacker logs in as admin after /createdb.
Login has no attempt limiting/lockout; combined with enumeration and weak passwords enables brute force.

must_not_report.reason: Non-vuln branch uses SQLAlchemy filter_by (parameterized); no injection.
jwt.decode pins algorithms=["HS256"] and verifies exp; no alg=none/alg-confusion (weakness is only the key, reported separately at config.py).
Non-vuln branch filters book by token user and title; ownership enforced.
Book owner is taken from token subject, not request body; no owner mass assignment.
Non-vuln branch updates the password of the token subject only, ignoring the path username.
update_email always modifies the token subject's record (path username ignored) in both modes; not an IDOR.
Delete requires the token subject's DB admin flag; function-level authorization is enforced (privilege comes only via the separately reported mass assignment).
Non-vuln branch returns a single generic error for bad username or password; no enumeration.
Non-vuln branch builds User without the admin field (defaults False); no mass assignment.

debatable.note: Flask/Werkzeug debug=True bound to 0.0.0.0; interactive debugger is PIN-protected, risk depends on deployment.
Non-vuln email regex [a-z0-9]+[\._]?[a-z0-9]+ backtracks quadratically (~0.4s at 20k chars, minutes at ~1MB body); authenticated, needs large input.
Unauthenticated listing of all usernames and emails; README describes it as intended "minimal information".
Unauthenticated listing of all book titles and owners (aids BOLA); no pagination (README "lack of resources").

Error JSON built by string concatenation (also user_model.py lines 28 and 76 for user records); stored email from register is unvalidated so response JSON can be malformed/injected, but served as application/json, no XSS.
Password change does not require the current password and existing tokens are not invalidated (both modes).
Registration schema imposes no password strength or email format constraints.
Container runs as root (no USER directive).
Third-party actions referenced by mutable tags (v2/v3) rather than commit SHAs; push-only trigger, no untrusted input.
